summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with nausea and left flank pain, found to have a left-sided pyelonephritis due to a malfunctioning nephrostomy tube. He had leukocytosis and acute-on-chronic kidney injury. The tube was draining pus, and urine culture grew Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, treated with a 7-day course of meropenem. He underwent two nephrostomy tube exchanges due to occlusion, with the second allowing successful capping. Hyponatremia developed due to excessive fluid intake and CKD, improving with fluid restriction to less than 2 liters daily. Renal function improved, with creatinine decreasing from 4.3 to 2.8. He passed the capping trial, was discharged home, and advised to follow up with urology, nephrology, and primary care, including a repeat CT for a known lung nodule.
